### `#047` — [JSOI2009] 游戏 (Bipartite Grid Token Walk Game)

- **Tier**: `Mastery 1 (Mas-1)` | **Judge URL**: [Luogu P4055](https://www.luogu.com.cn/problem/P4055)
- **Problem Summary**: Given an $N \times M$ grid ($1 \le N, M \le 100$) of `.` (empty squares) and `#` (obstacles). First, Player 1 (`YY`) chooses an initial empty square $v_0$ and places a token on it. Then, starting with Player 2 (`HH`), the two players alternately move the token to a 4-connected adjacent `.` square that has **never been visited before**. The player who cannot make a valid move loses. Determine whether Player 1 (`YY`) has a winning strategy, and if so, output **all** winning starting squares $(r, c)$ in lexicographical order.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Check Who Moves First After $v_0$ Is Chosen!"}
Player 1 (`YY`) only **places** the token on $v_0$; **Player 2 (`HH`)** makes the first move $v_0 \to v_1$! In the terminology of Theorem 4.1, is Player 1 the First Mover or the Second Mover in the walk game starting from $v_0$?
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Avoidable Vertices $V_E = L_1 \cup R_2$ via Residual BFS"}
Because Player 2 moves first from $v_0$, Player 1 (`YY`) is the **Second Mover** from $v_0$! By Theorem 4.1, Second Mover wins from $v_0$ if and only if $v_0 \in V_E = L_1 \cup R_2$ is an **Avoidable** vertex (omitted by at least one maximum matching). How do you find all $v_0 \in L_1 \cup R_2$ in $O(NM)$ time after a single Dinic run?
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Full 4-Step Compilation & Solution — Luogu P4055"}
#### Step 1: Non-Graph Diagnostic Signal (Recognition)
This is the canonical **Impartial Self-Avoiding Walk Game on a Bipartite Graph** (§4). Every orthogonal grid step flips chessboard parity $\phi(r, c) = (r + c) \bmod 2$, so the grid of `.` cells is bipartite. Furthermore, we must classify **all** $\le 10^4$ starting cells, requiring the $O(V + E)$ Coarse Dulmage–Mendelsohn BFS rather than $O(V \cdot E\sqrt{V})$ per-vertex rematching.

#### Step 2: Intermediate Algebraic & Logical Representation
Partition the `.` cells into $L = \{(r, c) = \texttt{'.'} : (r + c) \text{ is odd}\}$ and $R = \{(r, c) = \texttt{'.'} : (r + c) \text{ is even}\}$.
Since `YY` places the token on $v_0$ and `HH` moves first from $v_0$, `YY` is the **Second Mover** in the walk game from $v_0$. By Theorem 4.1:

$$
\text{YY wins by choosing } v_0 \iff \exists M^* \in \mathcal{M}^*(G) \text{ such that } v_0 \notin V(M^*) \iff v_0 \in V_E = L_1 \cup R_2.
$$

In particular, `YY` has at least one winning starting square if and only if $G$ does **not** have a perfect matching ($V_E \ne \emptyset$)!

#### Step 3: Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad (Mechanical Graph Compilation)
1. Build the unit bipartite matching network $N$:
   - $s \to u$ (cap $1$) for each $u \in L$, $v \to t$ (cap $1$) for each $v \in R$, and $u \to v$ (cap $1$) for adjacent `.` cells $u \in L, v \in R$.
2. Run Dinic to obtain maximum flow $f^*$.
3. Run Coarse DM Reachability (`DMDecomposition` from §5.1):
   - Forward BFS from $s$ along residual arcs with $c_{f^*} > 0$ marks $V_S$, giving $L_1 = L \cap V_S$.
   - Backward BFS from $t$ along residual arcs with $c_{f^*} > 0$ marks $V_T^{\text{rev}}$, giving $R_2 = R \cap V_T^{\text{rev}}$.
4. Collect all `.` cells $(r, c)$ in $L_1 \cup R_2$. If empty, print `LOSE`; otherwise print `WIN` followed by all $(r, c) \in L_1 \cup R_2$.

```cpp
// After running Dinic on S -> L -> R -> T:
vector<int> vis_S(T + 1, 0), vis_T(T + 1, 0);
queue<int> q;
q.push(S); vis_S[S] = 1;
while (!q.empty()) {
    int u = q.front(); q.pop();
    for (const auto& e : dinic.adj[u])
        if (e.cap > 0 && !vis_S[e.to]) { vis_S[e.to] = 1; q.push(e.to); }
}
q.push(T); vis_T[T] = 1;
while (!q.empty()) {
    int u = q.front(); q.pop();
    for (const auto& e : dinic.adj[u]) {
        // Backward arc v -> u has positive residual capacity iffdinic.adj[v][e.rev].cap > 0
        int v = e.to;
        if (dinic.adj[v][e.rev].cap > 0 && !vis_T[v]) { vis_T[v] = 1; q.push(v); }
    }
}
vector<pair<int, int>> ans;
for (int r = 1; r <= N; ++r)
    for (int c = 1; c <= M; ++c)
        if (grid[r][c] == '.') {
            int id = node_id(r, c);
            bool in_L = ((r + c) % 2 == 1);
            if ((in_L && vis_S[id]) || (!in_L && vis_T[id]))
                ans.emplace_back(r, c);
        }
```

#### Step 4: Hand-Checkable Toy Trace & Failure-Mode Guard
Consider a $1 \times 3$ path `. . .` at $(1, 1), (1, 2), (1, 3)$:

- $L = \{(1, 2)\}$ (odd sum $3$), $R = \{(1, 1), (1, 3)\}$ (even sums $2, 4$).
- Maximum matching size is $\nu(G) = 1$, say $M^* = \{((1, 2), (1, 1))\}$, leaving $(1, 3) \in U_R$ unmatched.
- Backward BFS from $t$: $t \leftarrow (1, 3) \leftarrow (1, 2) \leftarrow (1, 1)$ marks $R_2 = \{(1, 1), (1, 3)\}$ and $L_2 = \{(1, 2)\}$.
- Thus $V_E = L_1 \cup R_2 = \{(1, 1), (1, 3)\}$: `YY` wins by placing the token on either endpoint $(1, 1)$ or $(1, 3)$ (`HH` is forced to step to $(1, 2)$, and `YY` steps to the other endpoint and wins!).
- **Failure Guard**: Role-inversion (`FM-06B`)—outputting $V \setminus V_E$ instead of $V_E$ confuses `YY` (who places the token and moves *second*) with `HH` (who moves *first*).
- **Complexity**: Dinic in $O((NM)^{3/2})$ plus $O(NM)$ BFS ($< 15\text{ ms}$).
::::

### `#048` — [NOI2011] 兔兔与蛋蛋游戏 (Rabbit and Egg Sliding-Tile Game)

- **Tier**: `Mastery 2 (Mas-2)` | **Judge URL**: [Luogu P1971](https://www.luogu.com.cn/problem/P1971)
- **Problem Summary**: An $N \times M$ board ($1 \le N, M \le 40$) contains white stones `O`, black stones `X`, and **exactly one** blank space `.`. Rabbit and Egg play $K \le 1000$ turns ($2K$ half-moves): on Rabbit's turn, Rabbit slides an orthogonally adjacent white stone `O` into the blank space `.`; on Egg's turn, Egg slides an orthogonally adjacent black stone `X` into the blank space `.`. Given the transcript of $2K$ moves actually played, identify how many times Rabbit made a **blunder** (i.e., before Rabbit's move, Rabbit had a winning strategy from the current board state, AND after Rabbit's move, Egg now has a winning strategy from the resulting board state) and list their turn indices.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 1 — Why the Blank Space `.` Can NEVER Revisit a Square!"}
Track the movement of the single blank space `.`! Let the initial blank space at $(r_0, c_0)$ have chessboard parity $p_0 = (r_0 + c_0) \bmod 2$.

- On Move 1 (Rabbit), `.` swaps with an adjacent `O` at parity $1 - p_0$, leaving `O` at $(r_0, c_0)$ (parity $p_0$).
- On Move 2 (Egg), `.` swaps with an adjacent `X` at parity $p_0$, leaving `X` at parity $1 - p_0$.

Notice that whenever `.` leaves a square of parity $p_0$, it leaves an `O` behind; whenever `.` leaves a square of parity $1 - p_0$, it leaves an `X` behind! What stone color is required to **enter** a square of parity $p_0$ vs. $1 - p_0$?
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint 2 — Filtering the Board to the Valid Bipartite Graph & Online Vertex Deletion"}
To enter a square of parity $1 - p_0$ (Rabbit's move), that square must hold `O`; once `.` leaves it on Egg's move, it forever holds `X`, so `.` can **never** enter it again! Symmetrically, to enter a square of parity $p_0$ (Egg's move), that square must hold `X`; once `.` leaves it on Rabbit's move, it forever holds `O`, so `.` can **never** enter it again!
Thus if we keep **only**:

- $L$: the initial blank $(r_0, c_0)$ plus all squares of parity $p_0$ that initially hold `X`, and
- $R$: all squares of parity $1 - p_0$ that initially hold `O`,

the sliding-tile game is **100% isomorphic to a Self-Avoiding Walk Game** on the bipartite graph $G = (L \sqcup R, E)$!
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Full 4-Step Compilation & Solution — Luogu P1971"}
#### Step 1: Non-Graph Diagnostic Signal (Recognition)
At first glance, sliding stones changes the board configuration dynamically, which looks like PSPACE-hard Rush Hour / 15-Puzzle. However, tracking the **blank space `.`** reveals a strict parity-color alternation: `.` alternates between $(p_0, \texttt{'X'})$ squares and $(1 - p_0, \texttt{'O'})$ squares, and overwriting a square with the opposite stone color permanently locks that square out of future moves! This compiles the entire game into an online **Bipartite Self-Avoiding Walk Game** where vertices are deleted one by one along the game transcript.

#### Step 2: Intermediate Algebraic & Logical Representation
Let $(r_0, c_0)$ be the initial blank `.`, and let $p_0 = (r_0 + c_0) \bmod 2$. Define the active vertex sets:

$$
L = \{(r_0, c_0)\} \cup \big\{ (r, c) : (r+c) \bmod 2 = p_0 \;\land\; \text{grid}[r][c] = \texttt{'X'} \big\},
$$

$$
R = \big\{ (r, c) : (r+c) \bmod 2 = 1 - p_0 \;\land\; \text{grid}[r][c] = \texttt{'O'} \big\}.
$$

At the start of turn $t \in \{1, \dots, K\}$, the blank sits at $u_t \in L$, and Rabbit moves the blank to an unvisited neighbor $v_t \in R$ (permanently deleting $u_t$ from the graph); then Egg moves the blank from $v_t \in R$ to an unvisited neighbor $u_{t+1} \in L$ (permanently deleting $v_t$ from the graph).
By Theorem 4.1 (since the current player moves `.` **first** out of its current cell!):

- **Before Rabbit's move at turn $t$**: Rabbit has a winning strategy from $u_t$ in the current remaining graph $G_t$ if and only if **$u_t$ is Essential** in $G_t$ ($\nu(G_t \setminus \{u_t\}) = \nu(G_t) - 1$).
- **After Rabbit's move $u_t \to v_t$**: The remaining graph is $G'_t = G_t \setminus \{u_t\}$ with the blank at $v_t$. Rabbit's move was a losing blunder if and only if Rabbit could have won before the move ($u_t$ was Essential in $G_t$) **and** Egg now has a winning strategy from $v_t$ in $G'_t$ (**$v_t$ is Essential** in $G'_t$)!

#### Step 3: Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad (Incremental Online DM Maintenance)
How do we test whether the current vertex $x$ is Essential, and then permanently delete $x$ from the maintaining maximum matching `match[]`, in $O(VE)$ time per step?

1. **Initial Matching**: Build the bipartite graph $G = (L \sqcup R, E)$ between adjacent active cells and compute an initial maximum matching `match[]` via Hungary / Kuhn's DFS.
2. **Testing Essentiality + Deleting $x$ in One Step (`del_and_check(x)`)**:
   - Mark `removed[x] = true`.
   - If `match[x] == -1` ($x$ was already unmatched in our current maximum matching!), then $x$ is trivially **Avoidable** (not Essential), and deleting $x$ leaves the remaining matching maximum! Return `essential = false`.
   - If `match[x] = w != -1`, unmatch `w` (`match[w] = -1, match[x] = -1`) and run a single Kuhn augmenting-path DFS starting from `w` in the remaining graph (`!removed[.]`):
     - If an augmenting path from `w` is found, the maximum matching size of $G \setminus \{x\}$ did **not** drop ($\nu(G \setminus \{x\}) = \nu(G)$), so $x$ was **Avoidable** (`essential = false`)!
     - If **no** augmenting path from `w` exists, $\nu(G \setminus \{x\}) = \nu(G) - 1$, so $x$ was **Essential** (`essential = true`)!

```cpp
// Returns true iff x was Essential in the current graph, and permanently deletes x
bool del_and_check(int x) {
    removed[x] = true;
    int w = match_partner[x];
    if (w == -1) return false; // Already unmatched -> Avoidable!
    match_partner[x] = match_partner[w] = -1;
    fill(vis.begin(), vis.end(), 0);
    // If w can re-augment in G \ {x}, then x was Avoidable; else x was Essential!
    return !dfs_augment(w);
}

// For each turn t = 1 .. K:
// Blank is currently at u_t (Rabbit's turn):
bool win_before = del_and_check(u_t); // Deletes u_t and checks if Rabbit could win
int v_t = cell_id(rabbit_r[t], rabbit_c[t]); // Blank moves to v_t
bool egg_wins_after = del_and_check(v_t);    // Deletes v_t and checks if Egg wins from v_t
if (win_before && egg_wins_after) blunders.push_back(t);
int u_next = cell_id(egg_r[t], egg_c[t]);    // Blank moves to u_{t+1}
u_t = u_next;
```

#### Step 4: Hand-Checkable Toy Trace & Failure-Mode Guard
Look at how clean `del_and_check` is: when Rabbit moves $u_t \to v_t$, `del_and_check(u_t)` tests whether $u_t$ was Essential in $G_t$ **and** updates the maximum matching to $G'_t = G_t \setminus \{u_t\}$. Immediately after, when Egg is about to move from $v_t$ in $G'_t$, `del_and_check(v_t)` tests whether $v_t$ is Essential in $G'_t$ **and** updates the maximum matching to $G_{t+1} = G'_t \setminus \{v_t\}$ for the next turn!

- **Failure Guard**: Only include cells matching the invariant `(parity == p0 && grid == 'X') || (parity != p0 && grid == 'O') || initial_blank`. Including `(parity == p0 && grid == 'O')` adds unreachable vertices that corrupt the matching size!
- **Complexity**: Initial matching plus $2K$ incremental DFS augmentations on $|V| \le 1600, |E| \le 3200$ runs in $O((NM + K) \cdot NM) \approx 5 \cdot 10^6$ operations ($< 10\text{ ms}$).

## 7. Chapter 6 Verification Checklist & Failure Mode Summary

Before submitting any Hidden Bipartition, Dulmage–Mendelsohn, or Bipartite Game solution, run through this diagnostic checklist:

1. **Bipartition Invariant Audit**:
   - *Grid Leapers $(p, q)$*: Did you divide by $g = \gcd(p, q)$ first? If $(p/g + q/g)$ is odd, color by $(r' + c') \bmod 2$; if both $p/g$ and $q/g$ are odd (`Luogu P5030`), color by $r' \bmod 2$!
   - *Prime Sums $a_i + a_j \in \mathbb{P}$*: Did you deduplicate $1$s so at most **one** $1$ remains (`1 + 1 = 2` clique trap)?
2. **Obstacle-Split Strip & Coordinate Compression Audit**:
   - *Soft (`x`) vs. Hard (`#`) Obstacles*: Do hard walls `#` split row/column segment IDs while soft obstacles `x` neither split segment IDs nor generate edges (`#041`)?
   - *Discretized Grids (`#044`)*: Did you compress half-open intervals $[x_1, x_2 + 1)$ so unit widths are preserved?
   - *Hub Dualization (`#046`)*: Are leaf edges wired **bidirectionally** ($R_r \leftrightarrow C_c$, cap $1$ each way)?
3. **Dulmage–Mendelsohn & Game Role Audit**:
   - *Tarjan SCC Domain*: When classifying $\nu$-critical edges via $\operatorname{scc}(u) \ne \operatorname{scc}(v)$, did you include **both $s$ and $t$** inside the residual graph passed to Tarjan?
   - *Walk Game Role-Inversion*: Did you check whether Player 1 **moves first from $v_0$** (wins $\iff v_0 \notin V_E$ is Essential, `#048`) or **places the token on $v_0$ while Player 2 moves first** (wins $\iff v_0 \in V_E$ is Avoidable, `#047`)?

## 8. Chapter Revision Summary & Multilingual Bibliography

### Key Formulas & Structural Invariants

- **Coarse DM Partition ($V = V_E \sqcup V_O \sqcup V_U$)**:
  - $V_E = (L \cap V_S) \cup (R \cap V_T^{\text{rev}})$: **Avoidable** vertices (omitted by at least one $M^*$; never in any MVC; Second Mover wins in Bipartite Walk Game).
  - $V_O = (R \cap V_S) \cup (L \cap V_T^{\text{rev}})$: **Bottleneck Essential** vertices (in every $M^*$ and in **every** MVC).
  - $V_U = V \setminus (V_S \cup V_T^{\text{rev}})$: **Core Essential** vertices (in every $M^*$ and in **some** MVC).
- **Fine DM Edge Classification (Tarjan SCC on $G_{f^*}$ including $s, t$)**:
  - **Mandatory ($\nu$-Critical)**: $e \in M^* \land \operatorname{scc}_{G_{f^*}}(u) \ne \operatorname{scc}_{G_{f^*}}(v)$.
  - **Admissible (Allowed)**: $e \in M^* \lor \operatorname{scc}_{G_{f^*}}(u) = \operatorname{scc}_{G_{f^*}}(v)$.
  - **Forbidden**: $e \notin M^* \land \operatorname{scc}_{G_{f^*}}(u) \ne \operatorname{scc}_{G_{f^*}}(v)$.

### Multilingual Bibliography

- **`[EN]` Dulmage, A. L., & Mendelsohn, N. S. (1958)**. *Coverings of bipartite graphs*. Canadian Journal of Mathematics, 10, 517–534. (Foundational paper introducing the canonical $V_E \sqcup V_O \sqcup V_U$ coarse and fine block triangular decomposition.)
- **`[EN]` Lovász, L., & Plummer, M. D. (1986)**. *Matching Theory*. AMS Chelsea Publishing. (Chapters 3–4 develop the Dulmage–Mendelsohn and Gallai–Edmonds decompositions in full generality.)
- **`[ZH]` 胡伯涛 [Amber] (2007)**. 《最小割模型在信息学竞赛中的应用》 (*Applications of Minimum Cut Models in OI*). 国家集训队 2007 论文集. (Standard Chinese reference on bipartite conflict compilation, grid parity, and extremal minimum cuts.)
- **`[ZH]` 贾志鹏 (2011)**. 《二分图博弈及其在 NOI2011 兔兔与蛋蛋游戏中的应用》. (Introduces the online bipartite walk game reduction and incremental augmenting-path blunder check.)
- **`[JA]` noshi91 & maspy (2020–2023)**. *Dulmage–Mendelsohn Decomposition (`DM分解`) and Maximum Matching Criticality*. (Japanese algorithmic competitive programming treatises on $G_{f^*}$ SCC decomposition and lattice distance 2-adic coloring in `AGC 025 D`.)
